label: the same, the slab's face under friction
blurb: The same model after an earthquake of 5 m, with a law that is not linear on the slab's face: friction that strengthens with slip rate, at steady state, with a sigma = 1 MPa. Such a law has no Laplace state, so the face is stepped through time instead, the rest of the body reduced to what the face feels. It is the linear law of the model above for a small change of traction and faster above it, so it knows how large the earthquake was.
